function: Estimation of the direct and cascaded user-RIS-BS channels in a RIS-aided multiuser uplink, using a parallel-attention Transformer (EPformer) as denoiser (pp. 1, 4).
system: TDD uplink, K=6 single-antenna users, BS with M=32 antennas, passive reflecting RIS with N=32 elements, C=33 pilot sub-frames; carrier frequency not given (pp. 3, 9).
method: Transformer encoder-decoder with multi-head attention and super-resolution blocks (EPformer); supervised offline training with NMSE loss, then online estimation; no federated, meta, or transfer learning (pp. 5-7).
data_channel: Own simulator: Rician fading with distance-based path loss per [8]; 60,000 training, 10,000 validation, 10,000 test samples; no standard, public, or measured channel data (pp. 5, 9).
test_conditions: Default Table I setting (K=6, M=32, N=32, C=33); sweeps over SNR, pilots, RIS elements, mobility, and training-set size; testing outside the training setting is not stated (pp. 9-12).
baselines: Classical: LS [17] and MMSE [18]; learned: ChannelNet [38] and Interpolation ResNet [39] (p. 9).
metrics: NMSE (dB) versus SNR, pilots, RIS elements, user mobility, and training samples; offline training time and online estimation time (pp. 9-12).
complexity: Theta-order analysis Theta((2M(N+1))^2 d_k d_v) + Theta(2M(N+1)N_s h d_v) + Theta(2M(N+1)N_s^2) (p. 8); online 2.02 ms, offline training 660.02 s (Table II, p. 12).
q1_support: p. 9: "we include the Rician fading model to describe all relevant channels [37]". Own simulator with path loss per [8] (Table I); the paper never uses 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 9: "the training, validation, and testing sample numbers are 60,000, 10,000, and 10,000, respectively", all from the same simulator and setting (Table I). The sweeps over SNR, pilots, RIS elements, mobility, and training-set size (pp. 10-12) never state a model trained in one setting and tested in another.
q3_support: p. 9: "the LS method [17], the MMSE method [18], ChannelNet [38], and Interpolation ResNet [39]"; p. 10: "Obviously, our model outperforms all the other solutions" on NMSE versus SNR (Fig. 8).
q4_support: p. 8: "the overall complexity of the proposed EPformer-based parallel channel estimation model" is given in Theta notation; Table II (p. 12) lists online estimation time 2.02e-3 s and offline training time 660.02 s.
q5_support: p. 5: "we first generate CSI data using the Rician channel model outlined in Section IV". No code or data link, DOI, public dataset, or measured data is given anywhere in the paper.
notes: Included, area 2: channel estimation of direct and cascaded channels in a RIS-aided multiuser uplink with a Transformer denoiser. Tables I (p. 9) and II (p. 12) were read from page images. q2: Remark 1 (p. 6) says the model "can be readily adapted to various shapes" and Figs. 10-11 vary the pilots C and the RIS elements N, but the paper does not say whether one trained model is tested at other C or N or a new model is trained, so q2 is 0; the Generality Analysis (p. 12) covers user mobility and few-shot training only, and the few-shot test (Fig. 13) only reduces the training samples. q3: ChannelNet and Interpolation ResNet are earlier learned estimators; footnote 5 (p. 9) says Interpolation ResNet is applied to the RIS case.
